lines.text: My father met us at the water gate himself, after dark, with no torch and no guards. He looked years older than when I'd last seen him. So did I, probably.
You didn't run.
No.
No. You never did listen. Inside, all of you. Quickly.
He had brought Maric home by river the day after he woke. My brother was waiting in the hall, wrapped in a blanket like an old man. The white fire was gone from his eyes.
His thread was the hottest one I had. It felt like holding a coal.
I've thought of a great many things to say to you, little brother. They were all rude. I've decided to save them.
That's the nicest thing you've ever said to me.
Don't get used to it.
Over supper, I told my father everything. The vaults. The farm. And the woman chained to the great stone, who had known my name.
He couldn't stop looking at Nell. A hollow-born child at his table, eating his bread. He looked at her the way people look at a ghost.
His cup stopped halfway to his mouth, and stayed there.
Did she say anything else?
She said I'd got so tall.
My father put his cup down very carefully, as if it might break. Then he stood up and left the room without a word.
He's been doing that since I woke up. Leaving rooms. I've started timing him.
Later, I found him on the wall, looking north into the dark.
Greyhollow. Do you like it there?
It's home.
He nodded slowly, as if that answered something he'd been asking for years. Then, without turning, he said the strangest thing he ever said to me.
She would have been proud of you.
Who?
He didn't answer. He put his hand on my shoulder, once, the way you'd touch something you weren't allowed to keep. Then he went inside.
Maric told me, much later, that our father spent the rest of that night in the locked room at the top of the tower. The one with the painting.
I sent him north, like we said. To the cold, and to Bram. It wasn't enough. It was never going to be enough.
At dawn, a rider came up the Senn road at a gallop. A royal column was two hours behind him. And riding at its head was Brother Caddoc.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and fourteen, coming soon.
